methods.title: Catchment hydrology (land-cover pressure)

inputs.label: Watershed impervious cover
inputs.rationale: Impervious cover represents altered infiltration, runoff routing, and hydrologic flashiness.

inputs.label: Watershed agricultural cover
inputs.rationale: Agricultural cover represents a separate soil-disturbance, drainage, and runoff pathway that impervious cover does not capture.

breakpoints.label: 10% impervious
breakpoints.description: Boundary between the sensitive and impacted classes of the Impervious Cover Model (Schueler 1994).

breakpoints.label: 25% impervious
breakpoints.description: Boundary of the non-supporting class of the Impervious Cover Model (Schueler 1994).

breakpoints.label: 30% agriculture
breakpoints.description: Lower agricultural transition. Fish-index decline and subsidy-stress responses are reported above about 30 percent watershed agriculture (Allan 2004).

breakpoints.label: 50% agriculture
breakpoints.description: Upper agricultural screen. Habitat and biotic integrity decline become apparent above 50 percent watershed agriculture (Wang et al. 1997), aligned with NRSA reference-site screening practice.

limitations: The worse input governs because hydrologic alteration through one pathway is not offset by low pressure in the other.
Agricultural bands are national screening tiers, not ecological criteria.
A result computed from one input is labeled partial.

Sensitive macroinvertebrate taxa decline well below the 10 percent impervious Good boundary (community thresholds near 0.5 to 2 percent), so a Good rating is not a no-effect finding (King et al. 2011).

methods.title: Wetland extent

inputs.label: Woody wetland cover
inputs.rationale: Woody wetlands contribute surface storage and hydrologic attenuation.

inputs.label: Herbaceous wetland cover
inputs.rationale: Herbaceous wetlands contribute storage not represented by woody-wetland cover.

breakpoints.description: Lower national screening transition. Watershed wetland extents of 1 to 5 percent are associated with water-quality benefit and about 7 percent with flood attenuation (Mitsch and Gosselink, as reviewed by the Chesapeake Bay Program 2016).
Upper national screening transition, the top of the same reviewed 1 to 5 percent benefit range.

limitations: Natural wetland abundance varies substantially among regions.

methods.title: Road-density proxy for concentrated inflow pressure

inputs.label: Watershed road density
inputs.rationale: Road density is a directional proxy for concentrated runoff sources and hillslope-to-channel connectivity.

breakpoints.label: 1 km/km²
breakpoints.description: Lower STAF screening transition. It is not a demonstrated ecological threshold.

breakpoints.label: 3 km/km²
breakpoints.description: Upper transition grounded in NRSA least-disturbed-site road-density screening.

limitations: Road density does not count actual outfalls or establish whether runoff is treated.
The 1 km/km² breakpoint is a screening judgment.

USFS watershed-condition guidance classes road density more strictly (good under 1, impaired over 2.4 miles per square mile, about 0.62 and 1.49 km/km²), derived from salmonid watersheds. EASI keeps the NRSA-anchored national screen and discloses the stricter alternative.

methods.title: Flow alteration (degree of regulation)

inputs.label: Upstream normalized storage
inputs.rationale: Upstream storage is the regulated volume available to alter the natural flow regime.

inputs.label: Annual runoff
inputs.rationale: Annual runoff converts storage to a dimensionless degree of regulation relative to the river's annual water volume.

breakpoints.label: 2% DOR
breakpoints.description: Onset-of-regulation boundary. Comparative global assessment treats storage above 2 percent of annual flow as regulated (Lehner et al. 2011).

breakpoints.label: 15% DOR
breakpoints.description: Severe-regulation boundary. The free-flowing rivers analysis uses 15 percent as its operational pressure limit, the high end of a published 2 to 15 percent range (Grill et al. 2019). It is not a regulatory standard.

limitations: Degree of regulation does not describe operating rules, diversions, seasonality, or dam location on the network.
Missing or non-positive runoff is not converted to zero and leaves the metric unscored.

methods.title: Low-flow condition

inputs.label: Monthly flow variability
inputs.sourceField: NHDPlus V2 EROM QE_01 through QE_12
inputs.rationale: Population standard deviation of all twelve mean monthly flows divided by their mean. All months must be finite and the mean must be positive.

inputs.label: EROM mean annual flow
inputs.rationale: Mean annual modeled flow provides scale context; it does not determine the rating.

inputs.label: Expected NHD flow regime
inputs.rationale: Flow classification provides context for natural intermittency and does not determine the rating.

breakpoints.label: Reference index 0.39
breakpoints.description: Fair begins at an interpolated reference index of 0.39.

breakpoints.label: Reference index 0.69
breakpoints.description: Good begins at an interpolated reference index of 0.69. Physical crossings depend on the reference stratum.

sourceHierarchy.label: EROM monthly flow variability
sourceHierarchy.description: Use all twelve modeled monthly flows; missing or nonpositive-mean flow remains unscored.

limitations: Unvalidated screening proxy for low-flow condition. Agreement with the field wetted-channel measure was weak (0.18).
Monthly climatological variability is not a measurement of daily low flow, baseflow contribution, or wetted connectivity.
Level II curves compare variability with regional reference expectations; lower variability rates better. A national curve is the fallback.
All twelve months are required. Missing months are unknown, not zero. Natural intermittent and ephemeral streams require interpretation.

methods.title: Floodplain engagement (bank-height ratio)

inputs.label: Bank-height ratio
inputs.rationale: BHR directly measures the vertical separation between bankfull flow and the low floodplain surface.

breakpoints.label: BHR 1.3
breakpoints.description: Upper boundary of the functioning floodplain-connectivity class.

breakpoints.label: BHR 1.5
breakpoints.description: Boundary above which published stream-quantification guidance identifies non-functioning connectivity.

limitations: A BHR below 1.0 remains Good but requires geometry verification.
The DEM-derived cross section is a screening estimate and may require surveyed geometry.

methods.title: Floodplain access (entrenchment ratio)

inputs.label: Entrenchment ratio
inputs.rationale: ER directly represents lateral floodplain width available relative to the bankfull channel.

breakpoints.label: Reference index 0.39
breakpoints.description: Fair begins at an interpolated reference index of 0.39.

breakpoints.label: Reference index 0.69
breakpoints.description: Good begins at an interpolated reference index of 0.69. Physical crossings depend on the reference stratum.

limitations: National reference curves group channel slopes below 0.5 percent, from 0.5 to below 2 percent, and at least 2 percent.
An unsplit national reference curve is used when slope is unknown. Naturally confined valleys still require field interpretation.
Entrenchment ratio measures floodplain access; it does not establish channel stability or flood frequency.

methods.title: Hyporheic-exchange potential (channel gradient or sinuosity)

inputs.label: Channel slope
inputs.rationale: Slope sets the vertical hydraulic gradient that drives bedform-driven bed exchange, the dominant hyporheic pathway in steeper channels.

inputs.label: Reach sinuosity
inputs.rationale: Sinuosity indicates lateral exchange through meander necks and point bars, the dominant hyporheic pathway in low-gradient meandering channels. Because the better pathway governs, sinuosity understated by generalized reach geometry can only fail to credit lateral exchange, never lower the rating.

breakpoints.label: 0.003 m/m
breakpoints.description: Lower screening transition, carried over from the prior exchange-potential index. A screening judgment, not a published threshold.

breakpoints.label: 0.006 m/m
breakpoints.description: Upper screening transition, carried over from the prior exchange-potential index. A screening judgment, not a published threshold.
Boundary between straight and sinuous planform in common geomorphic classifications. A screening judgment, not a published threshold.

Boundary above which meandering is well expressed in generalized reach geometry and lateral exchange across bends is expected (Boano et al. 2006, Cardenas 2009). A screening judgment, not a published threshold.

limitations: Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is a co-dominant control that is unavailable, so steep reaches over bedrock or fine beds can overpredict exchange.
The better pathway governs because vertical and lateral exchange are alternative mechanisms. Either alone indicates exchange potential.

Sinuosity measured over generalized reach geometry understates planform sinuosity. Under the better-pathway rule that bias can only fail to lift a rating, never lower one. The earlier weighted slope and sinuosity composite was retired for exactly that downward bias.
A result computed from one pathway is labeled partial.
The slope and sinuosity bands are screening judgments, not published thresholds.

methods.title: Channel evolution

inputs.label: Bank-height ratio
inputs.rationale: BHR is a documented incision and floodplain-disconnection clue used in channel-evolution interpretation.

inputs.label: Entrenchment ratio
inputs.rationale: ER indicates lateral confinement and access to flood-prone width, another documented clue to adjustment state.

inputs.label: NHD feature classification
inputs.rationale: A canal/ditch classification is decisive. Other FCODEs are neutral and cannot imply stable condition.

breakpoints.label: BHR 1.3
breakpoints.description: Upper boundary for functioning floodplain connection.

breakpoints.label: BHR 1.5
breakpoints.description: Boundary above which incision/disconnection is Poor.

breakpoints.label: Reference index 0.39
breakpoints.description: Fair begins at an interpolated reference index of 0.39.

breakpoints.label: Reference index 0.69
breakpoints.description: Good begins at an interpolated reference index of 0.69. Physical crossings depend on the reference stratum.

sourceHierarchy.label: Documented channel-stage assessment
sourceHierarchy.description: A user-documented stable/recovered, moderately adjusting, or severely adjusting condition supersedes the proxy.

sourceHierarchy.label: Canal/ditch classification
sourceHierarchy.description: A canal/ditch FCODE is directly classified Poor.

sourceHierarchy.label: BHR and ER susceptibility proxy
sourceHierarchy.description: For other reaches, the worse BHR or ER index governs.

inputs.label: NHD feature classification
inputs.rationale: The NHD canal/ditch class directly identifies an artificial channel.

limitations: FCODE identifies channelization but does not quantify current geomorphic adjustment.

inputs.label: Documented adjustment class
inputs.rationale: The class records an integrated field interpretation of channel stage and active adjustment.

inputs.label: Observed indicators
inputs.rationale: Headcuts, bars, width/depth change, bank erosion, and recovery features support the selected class.

limitations: A defensible replacement requires a selected class plus a narrative identifying the observed adjustment indicators.

criteria.Good: Stable or recovered Stage I/VI condition
criteria.Fair: Moderate adjustment or recovery, generally Stages III-V
criteria.Poor: Severe incision or destructive adjustment, generally Stage II or severe III-IV

limitations: This is a susceptibility proxy, not a formal channel-evolution stage assessment. Both BHR and ER are required.
BHR retains its 1.3/1.5 bands; ER uses national reference curves by slope class, with an unsplit national fallback when slope is unknown.
Canal/ditch classification and documented field-stage overrides remain decisive. Naturally confined valleys require field interpretation.

methods.title: Bank erosion and armoring

inputs.label: Bank-height ratio
inputs.rationale: BHR is an established incision and floodplain-connectivity measure used here only as a susceptibility proxy, not as measured erosion or armoring.

breakpoints.label: BHR 1.3
breakpoints.description: Upper published functioning boundary, used here as the Good/Fair susceptibility transition.

breakpoints.label: BHR 1.5
breakpoints.description: Published non-functioning floodplain-connectivity boundary, used here as the Fair/Poor susceptibility transition.

sourceHierarchy.label: Observed erosion and armoring
sourceHierarchy.description: Complete user observations of both components supersede the proxy.

sourceHierarchy.label: BHR susceptibility fallback
sourceHierarchy.description: Used automatically when complete bank observations are unavailable.

inputs.label: Eroding bank
inputs.rationale: Percent eroding bank directly records the longitudinal extent of active erosion.

inputs.label: Armored bank
inputs.rationale: Percent armored bank directly records the extent of hard bank protection, which BHR cannot detect.

inputs.label: Annual bank retreat
inputs.rationale: Retreat rate may support interpretation but receives no universal class without a regional reference rate.

breakpoints.description: Lower EASI transition for observed erosion extent.
Upper EASI transition for widespread observed erosion. EPA's 30% moderate-to-marginal transition remains annotated context.
Any observed hard armoring moves the armoring component out of Good.
Half or more of the bank length armored is classified Poor. Armoring of 75% or more is annotated as pervasive.

limitations: The 5%, 50%, and 60% class limits are transparent EASI screening judgments. The 30% erosion and 75% armoring marks are interpretive annotations.
Annual retreat requires a regional reference rate and is supporting evidence only.

criteria.Fair: 5-<60% eroding bank or >0-<50% armored bank, with neither component Poor

limitations: BHR does not detect existing armoring and does not directly measure erosion rate or eroding-bank extent.
The DEM-derived cross section is a susceptibility screen and may require surveyed geometry.
BHR is reused by floodplain engagement and channel adjustment and is therefore correlated evidence.

methods.title: Sediment-supply potential

inputs.label: Agricultural cover
inputs.rationale: Agriculture represents the dominant disturbed upland sediment-source pathway.

inputs.label: Soil erodibility K-factor
inputs.rationale: K-factor represents inherent soil erodibility, the susceptibility term no other metric screens.

inputs.label: Road density
inputs.rationale: Roads are both a sediment source and a hillslope-to-channel connectivity pathway.

breakpoints.label: 30% agriculture
breakpoints.description: Lower agricultural transition (Allan 2004), shared with the land-cover pressure metric.

breakpoints.label: 50% agriculture
breakpoints.description: Upper agricultural transition (Wang et al. 1997).

breakpoints.label: K 0.25
breakpoints.description: Lower boundary of the moderate RUSLE erodibility class (silt loams).

breakpoints.label: K 0.40
breakpoints.description: Upper boundary of the moderate RUSLE erodibility class. Values above 0.40 mark the most erodible high-silt soils.

breakpoints.label: 1.24 km/km²
breakpoints.description: 2 miles per square mile, the properly-functioning limit in NMFS salmonid watershed criteria (as compiled in KRIS).

breakpoints.label: 1.86 km/km²
breakpoints.description: 3 miles per square mile, the not-properly-functioning boundary in the same criteria. Fine sediment in spawning gravels increases above about this density (Cedarholm et al. 1981).

limitations: The worse input governs. Source indicators are screened separately and are not summed.
Intrinsic soil erodibility (K-factor) can lower the rating in undisturbed watersheds. It indicates susceptibility rather than an active source.
The road-density bands derive from salmonid watershed criteria applied here nationally.
Agricultural cover and road density are also rated by other metrics and are therefore correlated evidence.
All three inputs are required. Missing inputs are not converted to zero.
Bank-derived sediment supply is not represented. The method screens watershed sources only.

methods.title: Substrate condition

inputs.label: Watershed agricultural cover
inputs.rationale: Agricultural cover represents a separate soil-disturbance, drainage, and runoff pathway that impervious cover does not capture.

breakpoints.label: 30% agriculture
breakpoints.description: Same Good/Fair boundary as the Catchment hydrology agriculture input.

breakpoints.label: 50% agriculture
breakpoints.description: Same Fair/Poor boundary as the Catchment hydrology agriculture input.

sourceHierarchy.label: Watershed agriculture share
sourceHierarchy.description: Crop plus hay cover from the active watershed evidence engine.

limitations: Watershed agriculture is a pressure proxy; it does not measure bed composition, embeddedness, or large wood.

Disclosed correlated pair with Catchment hydrology: the agriculture input and 30/50 percent bands are shared. The two functions have the same class on about 95 percent of analyzed reaches (rank correlation 0.94).
The substrate route is unvalidated. Natural slope and stream power strongly influence bed condition; field verification remains necessary.

methods.title: Thermal-regulation vulnerability

inputs.label: Woody riparian cover
inputs.sourceField: forest + shrub + woody wetland in 100 m corridor
inputs.rationale: Woody cover represents potential shade and thermal buffering. Grass and herbaceous wetland do not receive thermal-shade credit.

inputs.label: Watershed impervious cover
inputs.rationale: Impervious cover represents heated runoff and altered runoff routing.

breakpoints.label: 10% impervious
breakpoints.description: Lower impervious-cover pressure transition.

breakpoints.label: 25% impervious
breakpoints.description: Upper impervious-cover pressure transition.

breakpoints.label: Reference index 0.39
breakpoints.description: Fair begins at an interpolated reference index of 0.39.

breakpoints.label: Reference index 0.69
breakpoints.description: Good begins at an interpolated reference index of 0.69. Physical crossings depend on the reference stratum.

limitations: This screens thermal vulnerability from corridor shade and watershed impervious cover; it does not rate measured stream temperature.
Woody cover uses Level II reference expectations with a national fallback. Impervious cover retains its 10/25 percent bands.
Both inputs are required. Natural prairie and desert channels can meet regional woody-cover expectations with little cover.

methods.title: Organic-matter supply potential proxy

inputs.label: Riparian forest
inputs.rationale: Forest contributes woody and leaf-litter inputs.

inputs.label: Riparian shrub
inputs.rationale: Shrub cover contributes litter and low woody material.

inputs.label: Riparian grassland
inputs.rationale: Grassland contributes organic material in naturally non-forested settings.

inputs.label: Riparian wetland
inputs.rationale: Wetland vegetation contributes organic matter and avoids a forest-only bias.

breakpoints.label: Reference index 0.39
breakpoints.description: Fair begins at an interpolated reference index of 0.39.

breakpoints.label: Reference index 0.69
breakpoints.description: Good begins at an interpolated reference index of 0.69. Physical crossings depend on the reference stratum.

limitations: This estimates organic-matter supply potential, not CPOM retention or shredder condition.
All four source classes are required; missing classes are unknown. The capped sum is compared with Level II reference expectations, with a national fallback.

methods.title: Nutrient condition

inputs.label: Total nitrogen
inputs.rationale: TN represents observed nitrogen condition relative to the applicable NRSA region.

inputs.label: Total phosphorus
inputs.rationale: TP represents observed phosphorus condition relative to the applicable NRSA region.

breakpoints.label: Good/Fair
breakpoints.description: At or below the applicable NRSA Table 7-1 good/fair value is Good.

breakpoints.label: Fair/Poor
breakpoints.description: At or above the applicable NRSA Table 7-1 fair/poor value is Poor.

sourceHierarchy.label: Normalized WQP TN/TP observations
sourceHierarchy.description: Use valid total-fraction observations from stations within five miles and the preceding ten years.

sourceHierarchy.label: StreamCat CHEM integrity fallback
sourceHierarchy.description: Use when no qualifying TN or TP observation can be normalized.

inputs.label: Catchment CHEM integrity
inputs.rationale: The catchment CHEM component summarizes modeled chemical integrity close to the reach.

inputs.label: Watershed CHEM integrity
inputs.rationale: The watershed CHEM component captures cumulative upstream chemical-integrity pressure.

breakpoints.label: V 0.40
breakpoints.description: Lower EASI integration tier for the published CHEM integrity component.

breakpoints.label: V 0.70
breakpoints.description: Upper EASI integration tier. It is not an EPA nutrient criterion.

limitations: The CHEM component is a landscape-integrity fallback and does not estimate TN or TP concentration.
The 0.40 and 0.70 breakpoints are EASI integration tiers, not EPA ecological or regulatory thresholds.
Nearby monitoring stations are not necessarily reach-specific.
Each station is reduced to a median before station medians are combined, preventing heavily sampled stations from dominating.
One analyte may produce a partial rating.
When observations are unavailable, the CHEM fallback represents landscape integrity rather than measured nutrient concentration.

methods.title: Regulatory impairment

inputs.label: ATTAINS integrated-report category
inputs.rationale: ATTAINS is the authoritative national source for assessed-water reporting categories.

sourceHierarchy.label: Conclusive ATTAINS category
sourceHierarchy.description: Use an intersecting or qualifying nearby Category 1, 2, 4a, 4b, 4c, or 5 assessment.

sourceHierarchy.label: StreamCat CHEM condition fallback
sourceHierarchy.description: Use when ATTAINS is absent or Category 3 is inconclusive. The result is condition context, not a regulatory determination.

inputs.label: Catchment CHEM integrity
inputs.rationale: The catchment CHEM component provides condition context near the selected reach.

inputs.label: Watershed CHEM integrity
inputs.rationale: The watershed CHEM component captures cumulative upstream chemical-integrity pressure.

breakpoints.label: V 0.40
breakpoints.description: Lower EASI condition-integration tier.

breakpoints.label: V 0.70
breakpoints.description: Upper EASI condition-integration tier. It is not an ATTAINS category or regulatory finding.

limitations: This fallback changes the automated interpretation to water-quality condition context. It is not a regulatory impairment determination.
The 0.40 and 0.70 breakpoints are EASI integration tiers, not EPA regulatory thresholds.
Category 3 remains unscored because evidence is insufficient.
A nearby unit within 2 km is explicitly labeled nearby and may not represent the selected reach.
When ATTAINS is absent or inconclusive, the CHEM fallback is labeled water-quality condition context and not a regulatory determination.

The category mapping reflects remedy status, not severity. A Category 4a water is as impaired as a Category 5 water but has an approved TMDL, so 4a and 4b rate Fair as impaired-with-a-management-pathway. Category 2 means no assessed use is failing, which is weaker than Category 1.

methods.title: Habitat-support potential (woody riparian corridor)

inputs.label: Woody riparian cover
inputs.sourceField: forest + shrub + woody wetland in 100 m corridor
inputs.rationale: Woody riparian cover represents potential cover, wood recruitment, and bank-zone structure, the strongest desktop indicator of habitat support.

inputs.label: Reach sinuosity
inputs.rationale: Sinuosity indicates planform variability and is shown for context. It is not rated because sinuosity measured over the fixed assessment reach understates planform sinuosity.

breakpoints.label: Reference index 0.39
breakpoints.description: Fair begins at an interpolated reference index of 0.39.

breakpoints.label: Reference index 0.69
breakpoints.description: Good begins at an interpolated reference index of 0.69. Physical crossings depend on the reference stratum.

limitations: Corridor woody cover is a habitat-support proxy, not a field inventory of pools, wood, cover, or bedforms.
Level II reference curves account for regional cover expectations; a national curve is used when the regional curve is unavailable.
Naturally open prairie and desert channels may rate Good with little woody cover where reference expectations are low. Sinuosity is context only.

methods.title: Biological integrity

inputs.label: Predicted probability of Good BMMI condition
inputs.rationale: The published model predicts the probability that benthic condition is Good. It is not a measured IBI class.

breakpoints.description: Lower EASI probability-integration tier.
Upper EASI probability-integration tier. This is a modeled probability, not a measured class.

limitations: This is a modeled probability of Good benthic condition, not a measured MMI or multi-community IBI.
The 0.25 and 0.50 cutoffs are EASI integration tiers. The model is unavailable for about 59 percent of analyzed reaches; the disclosed ICI/IWI fallback remains.
The integrity fallback reuses landscape evidence scored by other functions and requires all twelve components.

inputs.label: Catchment hydrologic integrity
inputs.rationale: Published catchment integrity-product component.

inputs.label: Catchment chemical integrity
inputs.rationale: Published catchment integrity-product component.

inputs.label: Catchment sediment integrity
inputs.rationale: Published catchment integrity-product component.

inputs.label: Catchment connectivity integrity
inputs.rationale: Published catchment integrity-product component.

inputs.label: Catchment thermal integrity
inputs.rationale: Published catchment integrity-product component.

inputs.label: Catchment habitat integrity
inputs.rationale: Published catchment integrity-product component.

inputs.label: Watershed hydrologic integrity
inputs.rationale: Published watershed integrity-product component.

inputs.label: Watershed chemical integrity
inputs.rationale: Published watershed integrity-product component.

inputs.label: Watershed sediment integrity
inputs.rationale: Published watershed integrity-product component.

inputs.label: Watershed connectivity integrity
inputs.rationale: Published watershed integrity-product component.

inputs.label: Watershed thermal integrity
inputs.rationale: Published watershed integrity-product component.

inputs.label: Watershed habitat integrity
inputs.rationale: Published watershed integrity-product component.

breakpoints.label: V 0.40
breakpoints.description: Lower EASI integration tier applied to the lower published integrity product.

breakpoints.label: V 0.70
breakpoints.description: Upper EASI integration tier. It is not a measured IBI threshold.

limitations: ICI/IWI are landscape integrity products and are not measured biological assemblage condition.
Multiplication makes the result sensitive to every component and reuses landscape evidence scored elsewhere in EASI.
The 0.40 and 0.70 classes are EASI integration tiers.

sourceHierarchy.label: Published BMMI probability
sourceHierarchy.description: Use prg_bmmi0809 from the other area of interest within the published model frame.

sourceHierarchy.label: Published ICI/IWI landscape products
sourceHierarchy.description: When the BMMI model has no value, use the lower of the two complete integrity products.

methods.title: Invasive-species pressure

inputs.label: Established NAS taxa count
inputs.rationale: Established taxa records provide a transparent national indicator of invasive-species pressure.

breakpoints.label: 1 taxon
breakpoints.description: Transparent STAF transition from no established taxa recorded to recorded pressure.

breakpoints.label: 3 taxa
breakpoints.description: Transparent STAF transition to the upper count tier.

limitations: A zero count means no established taxa were recorded. It does not confirm absence.
HUC8 fallback results carry lower confidence than HUC12 results.
Count bands are STAF screening judgments.
Establishment status often cannot be confirmed from occurrence records, and uneven sampling effort inflates richness where effort is high (Mangiante et al. 2018).

methods.title: Nearby dam-proximity proxy

inputs.label: Mapped NID dams within one mile
inputs.rationale: Mapped dam proximity identifies potential longitudinal-connectivity pressure.

breakpoints.label: 1 dam
breakpoints.description: A single mapped dam within one mile changes the automated result from Good to Fair.

breakpoints.label: 2 dams
breakpoints.description: Two or more mapped dams within one mile rate Poor.

criteria.Poor: Verified adverse effect on aquatic organism passage within one mile

limitations: A mapped dam count is a proximity screen and cannot confirm passability or the severity of a barrier.
NID carries about 91,000 regulated dams while the National Aquatic Barrier Inventory maps over 500,000 barriers of all sizes, so zero mapped dams is frequently a false negative for passage.
Query failure is unscored, not Good.
